KS-2025-SB302.title: Requiring school districts to prohibit the use of personal electronic communication devices during instructional time and prohibiting any employee of a school district from using social media to directly communicate with any student for official school purposes.

actions.text: Died in Committee

Introduced

KS-2025-SB302.aiSummary: School districts and accredited nonpublic schools would have to set rules that stop students from using personal electronic devices during instructional time. It would also bar school employees from using social media to privately or directly contact students for official school purposes, with some exceptions and an option for approved school accounts. Schools would have to adopt these rules and report that they did so by September 1, 2026; virtual schools would not be covered.

KS-2025-HR6028.title: A RESOLUTION condemning the violent, aggressive, and hostile presence of United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

actions.text: Died in Committee
Referred to House Committee on Federal and State Affairs
Introduced

KS-2025-HR6028.aiSummary: The resolution would condemn the presence and practices of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and its related agencies, and honor people who died because of ICE enforcement actions or while in ICE custody. It would also call for an independent audit of ICE’s training, oversight, use-of-force rules, detention conditions, and accountability, with the findings released to the public. A copy would be sent to Kansas’s congressional delegation and some House members.

KS-2025-HB2707.title: Modifying the definition of abuse in the protection from abuse act to include certain acts or threats related to pets and specifying that courts may include orders relating to pets in protection from abuse act orders.

actions.text: Died in Committee
Referred to House Committee on Judiciary
Introduced

KS-2025-HB2707.aiSummary: The bill would change Kansas abuse protection rules to count threats or harm to a pet as abuse when done to control, punish, scare, or upset another person. It would also let courts include orders about pets in protection orders, including who has custody of a pet and keeping a person from harming or killing a pet. The changes would affect people seeking or facing protection from abuse orders, especially in households or dating relationships.

KS-2025-HB2473.title: Requiring all persons to be 18 years of age to be eligible to give consent for marriage and eliminating exceptions to such requirement.

KS-2025-HB2473.aiSummary: The bill would require anyone giving consent for a marriage to be at least 18 years old and would remove the current exceptions that allow younger people to marry with consent. It would affect marriage licenses and the people who can approve them in Kansas. The bill died in committee and did not become law.

KS-2025-HB2351.title: Amending the uniform arbitration act of 2000 to make certain agreements to appraise or arbitrate in contracts of insurance invalid and creating exceptions therefor.

actions.text: Died in Committee
Referred to House Committee on Judiciary
Introduced

KS-2025-HB2351.policyArea: Civil Procedure and Civil Actions, Insurance
KS-2025-HB2351.aiSummary: The bill would change Kansas law on arbitration in insurance contracts. For insurance contracts entered into or renewed after July 1, 2025, clauses that require appraisal or arbitration would not be valid, except for contracts between insurance companies, including reinsurance. It would also let a court decide if an agreement to arbitrate exists or applies.

KS-2025-HB2293.title: Prohibiting the acquisition of critical components of drone technology from countries of concern and the procurement of final or finished goods or services from countries of concern.

sponsor.name: Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development

actions.text: Died in Committee
Withdrawn from House Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development; Referred to House Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development
Referred to House Committee on Appropriations
Introduced

KS-2025-HB2293.policyArea: Contracts and Contractors, Municipalities, State Agencies
KS-2025-HB2293.aiSummary: The bill would bar state and local government agencies from buying drones or drone parts if the key parts were made in a country of concern or by a foreign principal, unless narrow safety and security exceptions are met. It would also stop state agencies from signing contracts for finished goods or services from a foreign principal, with some exceptions for certain deals tied to U.S. national security review. The limits would not apply to contracts already entered into before July 1, 2025, and the act would take effect when published in the statute book.

KS-2025-HB2009.aiSummary: The bill would make abortion illegal unless it is needed to save the pregnant woman’s life in a medical emergency. It would also let private people file civil lawsuits against those who perform, help with, or pay for a banned abortion. The measure would mainly affect abortion providers, drug sellers, and others who help with the procedure.
